class_rawmat_germanium.name: Germanium
class_rawmat_germanium.description: A brittle, grayish-white metalloid recovered almost entirely as a byproduct of zinc smelting and, secondarily, from coal fly ash. Not mined directly at scale. Major end uses are fiber optics, infrared optics, semiconductors and solar cells. Supply is highly concentrated in China, and Chinese export controls since 2023 have split the market into a low domestic price and a much higher Western price.

class_intermediate_gecl4.name: Germanium Tetrachloride (GeCl₄)
class_intermediate_gecl4.description: The dominant traded refined form of germanium — a volatile liquid deposited into silica glass preforms to raise the refractive index of optical fiber. Capability is China-dominant, with Umicore (Belgium) the main Western producer.

class_intermediate_geo2.name: Germanium Dioxide (GeO₂)
class_intermediate_geo2.description: Purified germanium oxide powder, used mainly as a polymerization catalyst for high-clarity PET plastic and as the precursor to other germanium forms.

class_intermediate_ge_metal.name: Germanium Metal / Crystal
class_intermediate_ge_metal.description: Zone-refined germanium metal and single crystal, transparent across the infrared band — the substrate for infrared lenses and windows in thermal imaging and targeting systems.

class_intermediate_ge_wafer.name: Germanium Wafers
class_intermediate_ge_wafer.description: Polished germanium wafers whose crystal lattice matches gallium arsenide, used as the base for high-efficiency multijunction space solar cells and some high-frequency chips.

class_component_optical_fiber.name: Optical Fiber
class_component_optical_fiber.description: Glass fiber that carries light signals across telecom and AI data-center networks; germanium tetrachloride is the dopant that makes the core guide light.

class_component_ir_optics.name: Infrared Optics
class_component_ir_optics.description: Lenses and windows that focus heat rather than visible light, used in thermal-imaging, night-vision, and targeting systems.

class_component_space_solar.name: Space Solar Cells
class_component_space_solar.description: High-efficiency multijunction photovoltaic cells grown on germanium wafers, used to power satellites.

class_component_pet_catalyst.name: PET Catalyst
class_component_pet_catalyst.description: Germanium dioxide used as a clean polymerization catalyst for high-clarity PET plastic.

dep_wulantuga.name: Wulantuga
dep_wulantuga.location: Shengli Coalfield, Xilingol League, Inner Mongolia
dep_wulantuga.deposit_short_description: Wulantuga is a coal-hosted (lignite) germanium deposit in the Shengli Coalfield of Xilingol League, Inner Mongolia, and is notable as one of the largest germanium deposits in the world by contained-germanium reserve size (~1,600 t Ge), with germanium concentrated in the #6 coal seam at roughly 137 ppm; germanium here behaves as an organically-bound trace element in lignite rather than a discrete mineral. It matters because, alongside the higher-grade Lincang deposit in Yunnan, it anchors China's coal-route primary germanium supply, which together with zinc-route recovery gives China ~83% of global primary germanium. The germanium-bearing lignite is worked as part of large-scale thermal-coal mining and power generation; germanium is recovered as a by-product from coal combustion ash, so output is set by power/coal economics, not germanium demand, and only an estimated ~15-25% of the theoretical contained germanium is commercially recovered. Current status is active/producing. The operator is Shengli Coal Group, a state-owned enterprise; ownership is treated as state-affiliated via the same group given the absence of public disclosure of any separate resource holder. Reserves are reported at the deposit level as ~1,600 t contained Ge (project-internal estimate, not USGS-verified in this run); germanium is the strategic by-product while thermal coal/power is the primary product, and contained-Ge recovery to refined output is estimated at ~20-35 t/yr. Specific offtake agreements for the recovered germanium concentrate are not publicly disclosed.

mine_wulantuga_shengli.name: Shengli Coalfield Host Operation
mine_wulantuga_shengli.location: Shengli Coalfield, Xilingol League, Inner Mongolia
mine_wulantuga_shengli.description: The state-owned coal mining and power-generation host operation that works the Wulantuga germanium-bearing lignite in the Shengli Coalfield; germanium is not mined directly but is concentrated in the fly ash / combustion residue when the Ge-rich #6-seam lignite is burned, and a specialist circuit leaches a crude germanium concentrate from that ash. Owner and operator are Shengli Coal Group, a state-owned enterprise in Inner Mongolia. It takes in germanium-bearing lignite/ash from the Wulantuga deposit (~27 t/yr contained Ge, derived midpoint of a 20-35 t/yr estimate). The process: burn the Ge-rich lignite for power, then recover a germanium concentrate from the resulting fly ash via hydrometallurgical leaching. It produces a crude germanium concentrate as the on-target output, plus thermal power and bulk ash as off-target products. The germanium concentrate flows on-target to Chinese germanium refiners that convert it to GeO2 and germanium metal; specific named offtake is not publicly disclosed.

refinery_chinese_state_ge.name: Chinese Germanium Refiner (Inner Mongolia feed)
refinery_chinese_state_ge.location: Inner Mongolia / China (specific site not disclosed)
refinery_chinese_state_ge.description: The domestic Chinese refining stage that converts the crude germanium concentrate recovered from Wulantuga (and other Inner Mongolia fly-ash sources) into refined germanium products; in the project intelligence this layer is the aggregate 'Chinese State Refiners' with limited public disclosure, focused on GeO2 and crude/refined germanium metal rather than fiber-grade GeCl4. Owner and operator are Chinese state-affiliated refiners; individual facility identity and ownership stakes are not publicly disclosed. It takes in crude germanium concentrate from the Shengli/Wulantuga host operation. The process: the crude concentrate is chlorinated/distilled and reduced/zone-refined to produce germanium dioxide (GeO2) and germanium metal. Output crosses out of the raw-material layer at the market/class boundary as refined germanium metal/GeO2 sold into the (largely domestic, export-licensed) germanium market. Specific commercial offtake agreements are not publicly disclosed.

co_shengli_coal_group.name: Shengli Coal Group (Inner Mongolia)
co_shengli_coal_group.description: State-owned coal mining and power group operating the Shengli Coalfield in Xilingol League, Inner Mongolia, where it works the Wulantuga germanium-bearing lignite. Germanium is a by-product recovered from coal-combustion fly ash, so the group's germanium output is policy- and coal-economics-driven rather than responsive to germanium prices, and is estimated at ~20-35 t/yr contained.

co_chinese_state_ge_refiners.name: Chinese state-affiliated germanium refiners (aggregate)
co_chinese_state_ge_refiners.description: Aggregate of smaller Chinese state-affiliated germanium refiners with limited public disclosure that process Inner Mongolia / Wulantuga and Yimin fly-ash concentrate into germanium dioxide and germanium metal. They focus on GeO2 and crude/refined metal rather than fiber-grade GeCl4, with combined output estimated at ~14 t/yr, and their output is subject to MOFCOM export licensing.
